minutes.headline: Finance Committee opened its budget public hearing and immediately continued it to March 26.
minutes.summary: The Finance Committee opened the previously-published public hearing on the budget and voted to continue it to March 26 at 7:00, because the tri-board meeting it was meant to follow had been moved. Anna raised concerns that the School Committee is obligated by bylaw to present its voted budget and explanation of major changes to the Finance Committee and public before town meeting, and that the board needs updates from the Select Board's budget workshop; the chair agreed to follow up with both. Members also discussed that both the school and town sides are expected to bring a core-services and a restoration/override budget rather than a single dollar figure.

public_comment.topic: A person who had joined the Zoom late (chair referred to them as 'Dave' or possibly 'Karen'/'Mr. Rogers') was invited to speak; the captions do not capture any comment content from them.

votes.motion: Open the Finance Committee's budget public hearing and continue it to March 26 at 7:00
votes.outcome: passed (roll call: Mike, Anna, Tanya, Jay, Tom, Jean, and chair all voted aye)

budget_items.what_was_said: Anna argued the bylaws require the School Committee to present the budget it actually votes to the Finance Committee, not just the single line item voted at town meeting. The chair said he had gone on the information available at the time and would ask the School Committee to bring forward whatever they voted.

budget_items.topic: Select Board / town manager budget workshop
budget_items.what_was_said: Anna noted the town manager and Select Board held a budget workshop where a lot changed, and the Finance Committee has not been given that updated information. The chair agreed to ask the town manager to share the latest snapshot of the omnibus budget.

budget_items.topic: Override vs. non-override budgets (school and town)
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair said the plan is still for at least two budgets each for the school and the town: one for a non-override scenario and one for an override. It was noted the School Committee could technically present only its single line-item vote and nothing more.

budget_items.topic: Cuts information tied to override vote
budget_items.what_was_said: Anna said residents need to know what a 'no' vote on the override actually means in terms of cuts, not just a dollar figure, so people can vote on something real.
The chair recounted that the tri-board straw vote discussed a core-services budget plus a restoration budget, and it appeared the town side was building a similar core-services/restoration split.

decisions.decision: Chair will ask the School Committee to bring forward and present whatever budget it voted, if it voted a balanced budget.
Chair will ask the town manager to ensure any Select Board budget discussions and the latest omnibus budget snapshot are shared with the Finance Committee.
The public hearing will likely remain open and be continued again as more budget information becomes available over the coming weeks.
Chair noted the School Committee's prior-night budget meeting video was confirmed (by 'Joe') to be posted to YouTube starting the next morning.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee opened its budget public hearing and voted to continue it to March 26 at 7:00.
A member said town bylaw requires the School Committee to present the budget it actually voted, with an explanation of major changes, not just a single line item.
The committee said it has not yet received an updated budget snapshot from the Select Board's own budget workshop with the town manager.
Both the school and town sides are expected to bring a core-services budget and a separate restoration or override budget rather than one dollar figure.
A member said residents need to know what a 'no' vote on the override would actually cut, not just see a total.

why_it_matters: Residents will eventually be asked to vote on an override, and this hearing is where the town and school budgets that frame that choice get explained before town meeting.
The bylaw question about the School Committee presenting its full voted budget, not just a line item, affects how much detail the public sees before deciding.
A continued hearing means the public comment window on the budget stays open into late March rather than closing now.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the one substantive vote (opening the public hearing and continuing it to March 26) and on the broad shape of the discussion, but our minutes miss several specific points the official minutes record — Ana Lockwood's bylaws concern about an unvoted balanced budget, her point about unshared workshop info, and Tom Gray's override/no-override suggestion — while our minutes add two items (a prediction about future continuances, and the YouTube-posting confirmation) that the official minutes omit entirely. The most useful thing for a person to check is whether Ana Lockwood's specific concern (a balanced budget must be voted before presentation to town meeting) was the actual basis for the chair's decision, since our minutes state a different-sounding rationale.
